claims.text: The material family of interest is multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys with BCC/B2 microstructures.
The primary mechanical response of interest is ductility, measured as elongation to failure.
BCC/B2 RHEAs undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during isothermal aging.
The non-monotonic ductility transition occurs during aging at 600–800 °C for approximately 10–100 hours.
Long-term annealing at 600 °C can substantially transform a superalloy-like BCC/B2 RHEA microstructure.
Aging increases the B2 phase fraction at the expense of the BCC phase fraction.
Isothermal aging progressively increases the B2 long-range order parameter.
Aging changes phase connectivity or crosses a percolation threshold in the ductile BCC phase.
An ordered, continuous B2 matrix provides high strength but poor ductility because of its ordered nature.
Restricted dislocation mobility in the ordered B2 phase is the mechanism responsible for the proposed brittle transition.
Further aging coarsens B2 precipitates and can establish a continuous BCC matrix associated with improved ductility.
Longer aging may restore ductility by activating additional slip systems in the ordered B2 phase.
Elongation will reach a minimum after approximately 20–50 hours and recover after more than 80 hours of aging.
The as-processed material has greater than 20% elongation because of a fine disordered or partially ordered BCC/B2 microstructure.
The transition is confined to BCC/B2 alloys with a valence electron concentration between 4.5 and 5.0.
Single-phase BCC RHEAs with VEC below 4.5 are intrinsically ductile.
Single-phase BCC RHEAs with VEC above 5.5 are intrinsically brittle.
Single-phase BCC and FCC alloys are not expected to exhibit the proposed non-monotonic aging response.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is an appropriate BCC/B2 dual-phase RHEA for the proposed falsification experiment.
Water quenching preserves the aged high-temperature phase fractions and ordering state.

contradictions.description: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is presented as a BCC/B2 RHEA satisfying the stated boundary, but the cited record identifies this alloy as an FCC/B2 eutectic HEA. Thus the proposed experimental exemplar does not meet the hypothesis's required BCC/B2 constitution.

NbMoTaW-based alloys are offered as examples of the multiphase initial state, while the cited evidence describes NbMoTaW as a BCC RHEA and supplies no evidence that it has the required BCC/B2 dual-phase constitution.
